title: 49 Days Adrift in a Floating Fishing Hut: The Full Case of Aldi Adilang
description:
Case 019, the full case file. In July 2018 Aldi Novel Adilang, 19, was working alone as the lamp keeper of a rompong, a floating fish trap shaped like a small hut, moored by a long rope about 125 kilometres off North Sulawesi, Indonesia. He had done the job since he was 16, for about 130 US dollars a month: every night he ran a generator to light the lamps that draw fish in, and about once a week someone came out to collect the fish and bring him food, water, cooking gas and fuel. The rest of the time he had a walkie-talkie. His employer was reported to have about 50 such huts. On 14 July the rope parted in high wind. It was the third time his hut had drifted; the first two times, after a week and after two days, the owner's boat had found him. This time the wind carried the hut, which had no engine and no paddle, north into open ocean. His supplies ran out, then his cooking gas. He caught fish and burned wood from the hut's own fence to cook them; he drank rain when it fell and, when it did not, soaked his clothes in the sea, wrung them out and drank that. He has said a shark followed the hut at one point, that he read the Bible he had on board every day, and that he thought he would never see his parents again. More than ten ships passed without seeing him. On 31 August, in waters off Guam, he waved at the passing bulk carrier MV Arpeggio, was not seen, and called it on his radio on a frequency a friend had once told him to use. The ship turned round and, in high waves, circled him four times; a rope thrown from it fell short, so he jumped into the sea and a crewman caught his hand. The crew gave him a towel, food and clothes, and the ship's cook cut his hair. On the advice of the coast guard on Guam the ship carried him on to its destination in Japan, where Indonesian diplomats met him at the port of Tokuyama on 6 September. He was home in North Sulawesi on 9 September, reported in good health, and has said he does not want to go back to work at sea. Rook didn't believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The hut, the supply boat, the sea, the ship, its bridge, the quay and the beach are generic low-poly sets, not models of the real rompong, the real MV Arpeggio, Tokuyama or his home village; no name, flag or logo appears on any of them. The young man, the boatman, the ship's officers and cook, the officials and his parents are simple figures and nobody's likeness is attempted. The charts are diagrams with invented coastlines and are not to scale. Staging details are reconstruction, not record: the time of day and the weather in each shot, how he caught fish, the fire in a tin, the stove, the jug held up in the rain, the cup, the look of the shark and where it swam, where on the raft he read, the lantern, the shape of the radio, who on the ship's bridge heard the call, the ship's ring round the raft, the rope ladder, the scissors, the gangway, the family's meeting on a beach, and the fish hook Rook keeps. Reports differ on his age (19 in most, 18 in some) and on the date he reached home (8 or 9 September). Drinking seawater is dangerous; the film shows what the reports say he did, not advice. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

authoring.run: scheduled long run, 17 Nov 2026; the oldest case in the ledger with a public or scheduled Short, a world3d.py and no long version
authoring.status_reason: ready (uploads as private for the owner), not approved: the film was reviewed from stills and low-resolution rehearsals only, with no playback at speed and no listening; the first full-resolution, 60 fps render is the cloud's; and the rehearsals failed the gate twice on movement before the film was restaged, so the margin on the real render is unproven. The three long-form videos before this one were shipped the same way. To publish it, the owner sets status to approved.

experiments.E1_E2: Spine v2 kept from the Short: the cold open is the rope parting, and Rook's doubt is spoken on the roof ridge with the black swell behind him (no office). The long version then goes back one week for 30 seconds (the job, the lamps, the weekly boat, about 50 huts), returns to the rope, and runs forward.
experiments.setup_shortened: plan/learnings.json asks long-form for a shorter setup and a stronger mid-video reversal. The background (job, pay, supplies, fleet) is 35 s of 193 s and is cut as 11 shots; the first reversal ('This has happened to him before. Twice. ... This time, no boat comes.') lands at 55 to 67 s.
experiments.rehook: 'Then, a ship.' at 102.3 s of 192.5 s (53%): after the Bible beat, the first chance of rescue arrives and sails straight past, four shots in four seconds.
experiments.hush: Shot 53 (the ship's bridge: the mate stops with a hand at his ear): the music drops out for 'On the ship, somebody hears him.' before 'And the ship turns around.'
experiments.rook_action: He leans over the side to look for an engine in the Short's shot; in the long version he counts the other huts' lamps from the roof and gives up (17), tests the cup of wrung-out seawater and tips it over the side (32), waves a rag of his own at the ship (39, 49, 75) and flaps along above the swim (60).
experiments.rook_mannerisms: Coin flip (8), shiny things: the lamps coming on (11) and the fish (14, 26), beak tap (21, 28), hat brim pulled down in the rain (29), over his eyes for the Bible beat (37) and when the ship sails past (41), a shed feather (34, 59), hat jump (26, 51, 54), both hands on his hat during the haircut (63), a touch of the brim on the quay and at the house (68, 70), pocketing the fish hook (76). He has no joke or gesture in the crying shot (44) and says he has stopped joking at 100 s.
experiments.ending: 'Case closed.' in the film. The Short's question (would you have kept waving?) is left for the Short.
experiments.thumbnail: Following the brief: one face at the moment of danger (he waves the cloth, mouth open) plus the object that tells the story (the hut, with the hull going past behind). Words: 10 SHIPS PASSED HIM, which adds to the title instead of repeating it. Checked at 168x94.

sound_plan.first_frame: One 'hit' at 0.07 s as a wave slapping the raft, a wave, then the rope ('cord') as it parts; no music sting.
sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: hook, tense for the doubt, calm for the job and the lamps, tense from the rope to the gas, calm for the fence, tense for the water and the shark, sad for the Bible, tense for the ships, sad for the crying, tense for day 49, action for the radio, wonder for the turn, tense for the circling, triumph for the jump, calm on board and to Japan, triumph for home, calm, end.
sound_plan.hush: The music is pulled out under shot 53 (the bridge).
sound_plan.tragic_beats: The Bible and the crying (95 to 103 s and 113 to 119 s) are 'sad' segments: no pulse, a low tone and a heartbeat only; Rook is still.
sound_plan.effects: Rope creaks on every loaded rope, splashes for water that is seen to move, ticks for counted things (lamps, ships, passes, scissors), a far horn for each ship, wind on the storm and rain shots. No effect is placed without a visible cause.
sound_plan.voice: Narration is ducked over the bed by the engine; the rehearsal measured it (see quality_gate), it was not listened to.

source_notes: Read for this run on 17 Nov 2026, through a fetch tool: the twelve pages listed, plus a CNN wire copy on CBS Detroit and a copy of the Jakarta Post story on The Star. Not readable: BBC and the Guardian's own page (the fetch was refused; the Irish Times page is the Guardian's article). The Short's facts were re-checked on these pages and stand. FACTS ADDED IN THE LONG VERSION, each with where it is stated. Lamp keeper since he was 16: AP (on Dawn), Irish Times/Guardian (his father), ScienceAlert, Wikipedia. His job was to light the lamps every night with a generator to attract fish: Jakarta Post 23 Sep, NPR (on KPBS), NBC, CNN. 'One of the loneliest jobs in the world' is the Jakarta Post's phrase; Rook says 'on earth'. Pay about US$130 a month: Jakarta Post 27 Sep (his own words: Rp 2 million, US$133), AP ($130 for hut minders). Length of contract differs (six months in most reports, a year in his own words on 27 Sep) and is not narrated. Once a week someone came to collect the fish and bring food, water, cooking gas and fuel: Jakarta Post, CNN, NBC, Irish Times, NPR. A walkie-talkie: Jakarta Post, NPR, Weather.com. The owner has 'maybe 50' rompong: Jakarta Post (consul general Mirza Nurhidayat), Irish Times, ScienceAlert. Third time adrift; the first time for a week, the second for two days, both times rescued by the owner's boat: Jakarta Post 27 Sep (his own words), AP, ScienceAlert, Wikipedia (quoting a BBC interview). That he waited for the owner's boat this time is NOT stated anywhere and was cut from the script; shot 21 (he looks along the horizon the morning after) is staging. Blown north: Jakarta Post ('far to the north'). Supplies meant for about a week and gone early: NPR (meant to last a week), AP ('my food ran out after the first week'), Jakarta Post and Irish Times (enough for several days); the script says 'only ever meant to last about a week. They run out.' Cooking gas ran out, then fence wood: Jakarta Post, NPR, NBC. Rain: AP ('When it didn't rain for days, I had to soak my clothes in the sea, then I squeezed and drank the water'); Wikipedia says he collected rainwater. The shark: NBC and TIME, both quoting his interview with TribunManado ('I could only pray that the shark went away'; TIME: 'followed by a shark', NBC: it circled). One original interview, so the narration says 'He says'. Where it swam and what it looked like are staging. The Bible: NBC ('read his Bible daily'), Irish Times ('had a bible on board'), Weather.com, Jakarta Post 27 Sep. 'He thought he would never see his parents again': AP ('I thought I will never meet my parents again, so I just prayed every day'), TIME, ScienceAlert. His thoughts of suicide (Irish Times/Guardian only) are not used, as in the Short. He waved clothes and lit a lamp at ships: NBC ('waved clothes and flashed lamps'), AP ('turned on a lamp every time he sighted another ship'), TIME. More than ten ships, none stopped or saw him: Jakarta Post, CNN, NBC, NPR, Global News (quoting the diplomat Fajar Firdaus). The radio frequency a friend had told him to use if he was blown away: Jakarta Post (and Weather.com, citing it); NPR says he tuned to the ship's frequency and that the chief mate heard 'Help Help Help' and told the captain; Jakarta Post says the captain caught the signal. The narration says 'somebody hears him'; the film shows a mate at a radio and a captain, unnamed. Circled four times, rope fell short, he jumped, the crew caught his hand: Jakarta Post, NPR ('four passes'; it adds a life preserver and a ladder), Weather.com. Towel, food, fresh clothes and a haircut from the ship's cook: Jakarta Post, NBC, NPR. The captain contacted the coast guard on Guam, which told him to take Aldi to Japan, where the ship was already bound: Jakarta Post, Irish Times, Weather.com; NBC says the ship was heading for Japan. Arrived Tokuyama on 6 September (six days after 31 August): Jakarta Post, CNN, NPR, Irish Times; Global News says Osaka, which is where the consulate is. Handed to officials of the Indonesian consulate in Osaka: Irish Times, Jakarta Post, CNN. A night in quarantine, the typhoon and the flight via Tokyo and Jakarta are left out. Home: he flew on 8 September and was with his family in Wori, Manado, on 9 September per the Jakarta Post, NBC and NPR; the Irish Times and Global News give 8 September. The narration says the ninth; the description notes the difference. 'In good health': Jakarta Post, Irish Times, Global News, NBC. He does not want to go back to work at sea: Jakarta Post 27 Sep ('wants to abandon the seafaring life', 'in search of a safer job'), TIME/AP (no longer wants to work on a rompong), ScienceAlert, Weather.com ('would start working on land'). Age: 19 in most reports, 18 in the Jakarta Post of 27 Sep and an AP caption; 19 is kept, as in the Short. Distance drifted is given as 1,200, 1,500 and 1,600 miles on different pages, so the narration keeps 'thousands of kilometres from home' (Jakarta Post, Global News). The time of day when the rope parted is not reported: 'at night' was removed from the narration; the night setting of the opening is staging, as in the Short. Things reported on one page only and left out: the missing GPS, compass and life vest and his uncle's briefing (Jakarta Post 27 Sep), his father's anger at the employer (AP), the fishermen's association call for trackers (NBC), the names of the ship's officers (NPR), a bamboo shower (Weather.com), a home-made spear (Wikipedia), singing hymns (Wikipedia, Jakarta Post 27 Sep). Staging that is not fact: every set's look; the supply boat and the boatman; how many lamps; fish visible at the surface; the stove; the jug held up in the rain; the cup; the lantern; the ship's lights; the bridge and who is on it; the ring the ship draws; the gangway and the quay; the two officials; the meeting with his parents on a beach in front of a stilt house (reports say only that he was back with his family in Wori); his walk up the beach.

quality_gate.access: What was inspected: low-res contact sheets of every 3D shot (three rounds), the composited flat cards, the thumbnail at full size and at 168x94, five frames at 1280x720 and 20 samples, and three full-length rehearsals (384x216, 4 samples, 6 fps 3D frames composited at 12 fps with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound) reviewed as a 4-frames-per-second sheet of the whole video (770 frames). Not done: no playback at speed, and the audio was measured, not listened to. The cloud render is the first full-resolution, 60 fps pass.
quality_gate.method: Rounds 1 and 2 (contact sheets, 67 3D stills each). Found and fixed: Rook cut off the top of the frame and the young man off the bottom in the Short's portrait framing of shot 3; the walkie-talkie covering his face; the rope not in frame in the close shot of the post; Rook lost in the dark doorway in the morning-after shot; the jug in front of his face in the rain; the shark too dark and too far in both shark shots; the lantern shot hidden behind a lamp pole; the night raft too dark to read; the hut a speck in the shot from above the ship; the bridge shot showing only the captain's back; the swimmer's Rook out of frame; Rook hidden behind the young man on the quay and on the beach; the thumbnail's ship out of frame. Round 3 (cards and overlays at full size): a label running off the left edge on three charts, 'DAY 49' over a date, a heading over the number 16. Rounds 4 and 5 (full rehearsals with the gate). The first two rehearsals FAILED the gate locally on static stretches (15 to 22 s, 44 to 47 s, 125 to 129 s, 175 to 181 s) and a weak first second: long shots on a calm sea barely change from frame to frame. Fixed in the film, not in the gate: every shot now swings round its own subject and eases in; the establishing shot circles the raft at deck height; Rook walks the deck with his coin instead of standing; the beach walk is a side-on tracking shot past the house and palms; the charts have moving sea and wind; the opening pushes in harder. Round 6 (4 fps sheet of the whole video): his face was under the caption band in shot 3, a gantry leg crossed the lens at the start of the quay shot, 'NO BOAT COMES' sat on the track, 'PASS 1 OF 4' touched the left edge; all fixed. Round 7: the mate's arm crossed his face on the bridge and the bridge's back wall was bare; fixed, and the last rehearsal was rendered again from the final files.
quality_gate.gate_result: Last rehearsal, rendered from the final files: local gate PASS. 76 shots, mean 2.53 s, longest 3.71 s, first shot 2.35 s; Rook acting in 34 of 76 shots (45%); -14.5 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, voice 16.5 dB over the bed; closest match to any earlier episode 0.83 (shot 43, the ships card, against r003-lemons-long; the limit is 0.93); mean frame change 2.42; first second 2.21 (floor 2.0); lowest 3.5 s stretches without a detected cut: 1.09 at 25.3 s, 1.22 at 18.0 s, 1.5 at 44.0 s (floor 0.8). Duration 192.5 s (3 min 13 s). The rehearsal's fingerprint file was deleted, not committed; the cloud render runs the real gate at 1280x720 and 60 fps.
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D or scenes.SHOTS (by script); HOST lists every kind in which Rook is placed (34 of 76 shots, 45%); no kind is used more than three times (wave_cloth, from three angles) and none twice in a row; 62 kinds in 76 shots. First shot 2.35 s; longest 3.7 s; mean 2.53 s. Re-hook at 53%. One hush shot (53). Every on-screen date, name and figure was checked against the sources: JULY 2018, ALDI NOVEL ADILANG, 19, 125 KM FROM LAND, NORTH SULAWESI, SINCE HE WAS 16, ABOUT $130 A MONTH, ONCE A WEEK, ABOUT 50 HUTS, 14 JULY 2018, 1ST TIME ADRIFT A WEEK, 2ND TIME ADRIFT TWO DAYS, FOUND, DAY n ADRIFT, 10+ SHIPS, NONE STOPPED, SEVEN WEEKS, 31 AUGUST 2018, DAY 49, GUAM, MV ARPEGGIO, PASS n OF 4, TOKUYAMA, 6 SEPTEMBER 2018, JAPAN, 9 SEPTEMBER 2018, 49 DAYS. The charts are marked DIAGRAM, NOT TO SCALE and use invented outlines. Nothing graphic is shown and nobody dies in this story; the shark is a fin and a shape and touches nothing; the crying and Bible beats have no joke; his thoughts of suicide, reported on one page, are not mentioned. No flag, emblem, logo, lettering or likeness appears on any set, ship or person.
quality_gate.not_met: Loudness range measures 2.7 LU (ffmpeg ebur128) against the checklist's 4 LU; this is the engine's mix and earlier approved episodes measure about the same. No playback and no listening. Preview stills were looked at at 640x360 and in the rehearsal at 384x216; only five frames at 1280x720. The 13-category score is from stills and the rehearsal sheets. The gate's margin on movement is thin in two places in the rehearsal (the lowest 3.5 s stretch without a detected cut is listed in gate_result against a floor of 0.8), and the cloud render is cleaner than the rehearsal, so the real gate could still fail there; if it does, the fix is more movement in those shots, not a change to the gate.

review.weakest: The swimmer lies flat like a plank (60); the hut is small in the shot from above the ship (48) and in the two high dawn shots (6, 22); the night ship (42) is dark; the bridge is a plain room; the low-poly figures' hands cannot hold things convincingly (the book, the scissors, the radio); several day shots share one look (same raft, same sky), which the camera movement relieves but does not cure. Narration and sound were measured, not heard.
